question: Recent investigations1 have reported that members of the royal family of the United Arab Emirates (UAE) – a country with a human rights record that Parliament has formally condemned2 – received more than EUR 71 million in common agricultural policy (CAP) subsidies between 2019 and 2024, through 110 payments traced to companies and subsidiaries controlled by the Al Nahyan family, for landholdings in Romania, Italy and Spain.

Under existing disclosure requirements, only direct recipients of subsidies are named, making it difficult to identify the ultimate beneficiaries. This raises concerns about whether these payments comply with the eligibility and management control requirements of Regulation (EU) 2021/21163. 1.

Does the Commission consider this situation an infringement of Regulation (EU) 2021/2116, and what measures will it take to prevent CAP funds from benefiting ultrawealthy beneficiaries from non-EU countries through complex corporate structures?

What tracing mechanisms exist at EU level to identify the ultimate beneficiaries of CAP funds, and would the Commission consider introducing mandatory beneficial ownership disclosure as part of the 2028 CAP reform, and commit to publishing such data in a complete and accessible format?

Where CAP payments have been obtained through opaque structures or arrangements contrary to CAP objectives, will the Commission investigate and seek recovery of unduly paid funds under Regulation (EU) 2021/2116?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (10.9.2026) Current rules on the eligibility of direct payments from the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) require CAP beneficiaries to be active farmers, but do not contain provisions at EU level excluding beneficiaries referred to in the question. Under shared management, the Commission is not involved in payments to final beneficiaries.

This is the Member States’ role and responsibility. Member States have to put in place management and control systems. The Commission assesses whether these systems function properly. Information about beneficiaries of the CAP and their identification is made public by Member States as required by Regulation (EU) 2021/21161. The identification of beneficial owners is not required by the current Regulation.

Under the proposed 2028-2034 Multiannual Financial Framework, the Financial Regulation, in combination with the proposed sector-specific rules, would require the collection of information on beneficial owners2. For such future CAP rules3, the Commission considers that support should go to farmers whose principal activity is agriculture.

In addition to the eligibility linked to agricultural activity, the Commission’s proposal for the next CAP states that the total annual amount of degressive area-based income support would be reduced for payments exceeding EUR 20 000 and capped at EUR 100 000 per year. These provisions, as proposed, address the risk that income support goes to entities whose principal business activity is not farming.

The proposal is currently under negotiation by the co-legislators. In a shared management system such as the CAP financing, national authorities should ensure that the CAP funds are distributed in line with the applicable legislation. The Commission has tools to protect the Union’s financial interests if irregularities have not been adequately addressed.

When the Commission becomes aware of any suspected case of fraud, corruption or illegal activity affecting the EU budget, it informs the European Anti-Fraud Office and/or the European Public Prosecutor’s Office in accordance with applicable EU legislation.
